summary: Leelanau tower near Maple City, called the Cedar tower in 1937 and 1955 papers; moved there in 1928, staffed 1930-1956; no fate or current site found.

events.note: Moved from a hill north of Glen Lake to its present location, per a 1937 Leelanau Enterprise item.
A towerman, Fred Ensign, is named as working the Leelanau tower near Maple City.
Towerman sighted a forest fire in Mason County from the tower, 61 miles away.
Leelanau County Times, March 1948: the tower was manned during all fire weather.
March 1953: the county had no watchman for the tower yet and no fire officer for the year.
August 1955: the tower near Maple City was manned seven days a week.
April 1956: a watchman was appointed for the conservation department's tower near Maple City for that season.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1937 item puts the tower on a hill south of Maple City. A 1955 item puts the Cedar Fire Tower one mile east of Maple City. Left open.
The 1937 and 1955 items call the tower near Maple City the Cedar tower, so the Maple City record and the Cedar page appear to describe one tower.

notes_for_editor: Height converted from 82 feet (25.0 m). Staffing events are from dated newspaper items quoted on two compiler pages. The Cedar page is treated as the same tower; no separate Cedar record exists under data/towers/mi, so consider adding Cedar tower to other_names or merging. The location conflict (south vs one mile east) is not resolved. No fate after April 1956 and no current-site source found. Leelanau Historical Museum search returned HTTP 403 when fetched.
